## Result

- Skill: design-review
- Review status: changes-requested
- Package members: release — docs/design/release/release.md; system — docs/design/system/system.md; design — docs/design/design/design.md; published-skill-first-release-amendment — specs/published-skill-first-repository-simplification.md. Exact package and relied-on contextual subjects are stored.
- Upstream review ID: proposal-review-r4, approved/current; it renews unchanged proposal-review-r3 direction against the two amended contextual sources. R3 remains stale on its original subjects.
- Review ID and round: design-review-r3, round 3.
- Material findings: design-r3-f1.
- Correction targets: release; design authoring.
- Recording status: recorded through targeted batch on successful save.
- Open blockers: no missing direction authority; one concrete required design correction prevents approval.
- Immediate next stage: owning Design correction through Route; no Delivery reliance yet.
- Claim limitations: assesses selected behavior and source transfer, not implemented orchestration, remote environment configuration, successful publication, Verify or PR readiness.

## Package assessment

The amended proposal changes the objective substantively. This review assesses one normal maintainer approval followed by automatic preparation/checking/publication/observation/reporting, candidate-specific authority, explicit duration-telemetry consequences and source consolidation. Earlier source-only approval is not relied upon for these new behaviors. Current Proposal Review r4 supplies renewed direction authority; current context and exact subject inspection establish the reviewed basis.

The model now clearly assigns normal work to CLI/CI and reserves one candidate-specific authorization for the maintainer. The source/version/summary policy uses reviewed merged next-version input and established configuration rather than invented version intent; missing decisions are explicit upstream exceptions. This avoids requiring routine profile assembly, metadata copying or helper sequencing. It does not promise that every merge is releasable or that setup and genuine recovery decisions disappear.

The bounded coordinator, protected executor, immutable retained candidate, explicit S/C derivation limit and separate post-publication evidence are credible architectural choices, subject to the finding below. One protected executor contains downstream writes/observation/reporting, avoiding a second normal approval. Approval includes source, artifacts, destinations and workflow/check basis; stale/mismatched inputs fail. Duplicate approval and uncertain writes inspect authoritative external state rather than blindly publish again. Matching public results support observation, and partial results preserve successful external writes. The evidence ref has automatic compare-and-swap preservation, pre-write pending/approval persistence and recoverable reporting failure; it does not require a maintainer commit/merge on the normal path. Its reader integration and configured permissions are explicit Delivery dependencies, not claims that remote setup exists.

GitHub's linked deployment environment documentation was checked for the selected feasibility claim: required reviewers gate jobs and environment secrets become available after approval. This supports using one protected executor, not automatic candidate-byte binding or proof of actual repository configuration. Candidate retention and explicit executor verification remain necessary. Source: [GitHub deployment environments](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments).

Timing policy is now an explicitly approved change: absent telemetry does not block an otherwise correct routine release, malformed emitted data still fails diagnostic format validation, and actual identity/check/event facts remain mandatory. The model and displacement map name the affected R39–42/test consequences and direct consumers; no skipped-failure shortcut or silent restoration of the older timing gate is selected. Original design-r1-f2 remains resolved about its historical subject; the new direction permits this later explicit amendment. The narrower routine-automation population from design-r1-f1 remains preserved.

System composes the new actor and identity relationships; the R7/R8 legacy amendment remains new-profile-only, preserving its protective obligations and historical remainder while explicitly selecting bounded coordination/timing consumer changes. Design retention applicability is unchanged. The six-source retirement and mixed architecture boundaries remain precise; operational schemas, historical literal baseline, fixtures and prior evidence remain necessary consumers. Existing helper entrypoints, tag workflow, profile/notes generation, validators, package metadata and evidence-ref readers are allocated as actual integration surfaces. No new general engine or other model migration is required.

All representative scenario dimensions and integrated hazards remain meaningful. Complete-path fixture proof must exercise the actual coordinator and real required validators around substituted public services, including authorization, failed prerequisite, stale candidate, uncertain/partial write, unavailable timing, failed smoke and evidence-persistence failure. The package appropriately distinguishes fixture evidence from hosted/public success and retains fresh final whole-change Code Review and distinct Verify.

Optional traceability refinement: the new full-path and candidate/observation scenarios should also cite REL-SR-22–24 directly in their Requirement basis cells. The requirements and explicit Quality/Runtime allocations already describe these obligations, so this is advisory rather than a second material finding.

## Independence and inspection limits

The original independent reviewer did not author this amendment or any member. Reviewed the complete Release model including its summary graph, candidate/executor/evidence architecture and changed ownership/timing maps; assessed unchanged full member content from prior complete inspection together with exact current deltas. Read current amended proposal and renewed independent upstream assessment. Prior complete six-source and ADR-meaning inspection remains relevant to unchanged source-retirement scope; the amended runtime design received fresh assessment. Bounded inspection of actual package metadata reader, local candidate metadata generation and baseline release workflow supplies the finding's consumer basis. No whole-repository conformance, implementation pass or public operation is claimed. No project-map reliance was needed.

Commands actually used: git diff/stat and bounded source reads/searches; primary context with full selected records; subject inspect for all stored subjects; official linked GitHub documentation read; purpose-specific help already read for this same reviewer; targeted batch. No release, package build, live smoke or runtime test was run. Structural record validation and git diff --check follow the save. Review writes only its own judgment/findings/applicability; no engineering, activity/work, commit or external writes.

## Finding design-r3-f1

- Finding ID: design-r3-f1
- Severity: Major
- Location: docs/design/release/release.md — Routine coordination and immutable candidate, paragraph beginning Let S; Authoritative facts and consumer reconciliation.
- Finding scope: artifact-local
- Affected artifact IDs: release
- Owning stages: design
- needs-decision rationale: none; approved scope permits the necessary build/consumer correction.
- Evidence: The Routine coordination and immutable candidate paragraph seals C before building the package/archives and says metadata describing their hashes and C is produced afterward outside C. That leaves out the metadata that must be inside the npm package before it is sealed: packages/rigorloop/dist/bin/rigorloop.js loadVerifiedBundledMetadata requires releases.json to name a bundled adapter metadata file and its SHA-256, then verifies that file before installation. adapter_distribution.py _prepare_local_cli_release_candidate demonstrates the real dependency by deriving adapter metadata from already-built archives and writing its index before supplying the package candidate. Treating all hash metadata as post-package evidence either packages pending/stale metadata, requires a later repack of the supposedly immutable tarball, or leaves Delivery to invent an undeclared build overlay/identity boundary. The generic consumer-inspection row does not resolve the contradictory selected ordering.
- Required outcome: Define the dependency order explicitly: sealed source basis, adapter archives, current package-bundled archive metadata and releases index, npm packing and packed-candidate checks, then outer tarball/approval/evidence metadata. Distinguish package build outputs from post-build observations and identify any generated staging overlay allowed outside C, its derivation inputs and its binding into the approved candidate. Neither C nor a tarball must contain its own final digest. Preserve exact-byte publication and actual installation metadata checks; no new Distribution/Installation model or manual hash work is required. Add or reference a composed outcome that catches stale/missing bundled metadata despite valid standalone archives.
- Safe resolution path: amend the Release build/identity contract and composed outcome, then return the exact package for independent reassessment before Delivery. No runtime rewrite or source deletion is requested at this stage.
